checks: Ran the archived verifier outside the checkout and independently checked the raw rational data. There are 399 distinct index triples in range with positive masses totaling one. The first and combined second/third marginal identities hold at all 200 indices. A separate direct recomputation of the three symmetrized arrays gave (2r+1)/40000 for each array and each index.

The integer weighted upper-endpoint score has maximum 546 and is saturated by 141 positive-mass triples. Exchanging the second and third indices preserves that score. In the continuum lift the bound 546/200=273/100 is the essential supremum if the conditional draws are chosen independent, since saturated bins have positive mass and positive density arbitrarily near their upper endpoints. Only the upper bound is needed in the candidate.

Each conditional bin density is 2v divided by its bin mass, so mixing with the verified bin weights gives the exact density 2v on [0,1] for every coordinate. This verifies the continuous law without an interpolation approximation.

The stated a scales the weighted support bound to Σ_i W_i≤1. Adding all residual mass to W_1 gives a nonnegative simplex point and coordinatewise domination. For each t>0, the scaled Beta CDF is min(1,(t/a_i)^2), so P(Z_i≤t)≤(t/a_i)^2 and the capacity infimum over positive CDFs is at least a_i.

Independent Fraction arithmetic gives Σ_i a_i²+2∏_i a_i−1=33583/20346417 and the polynomial evaluated at p=(200/273,1,1) equal to −142/74529. The predecessor implies a∉D_2 and downward closure excludes the resulting capacity vector, which dominates a.

dependencies.application: At d=2 the frozen predecessor applies to this exact D_2 and nonnegative a. It supplies both the necessary polynomial test at nonnegative p and the equivalent cubic criterion, as well as downward closure for transferring exclusion to the capacity vector.

overlap.comparison: The accepted planar cubic region under f=2v overlaps the exclusion inequality, and comes from ordinary strict triangle cap geometry. Its hypotheses neither construct an arbitrary simplex law nor show the capacity bound for such a law can fail.

readability: The last two index marginals are summed with multiplicity. If the same index occurs in both positions it contributes twice before the fair exchange, as in the archived verifier.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The exact rational certificate gives continuous Beta(2,1) marginals with the required joint support bound. Adding residual mass to the first coordinate yields a simplex law with capacities at least a, and two exact tests exclude a from D_2, subject to admission of the frozen support-dual predecessor.
